scores.round_files_fidelity_rationale: Down from 6.3, mainly for the compile error. Good: fft.rs follows fft.cs statement by statement. It keeps the 1 << (int)logN mask (i32::wrapping_shl), uint BitReverse with shifted-out bits, the int-wrapping and truncating FreqTable with OverflowException on a negative size, the 4/N Hanning, double.Epsilon as f64::from_bits(1) (the smallest subnormal, not machine epsilon), the copy order (re then im) before an IndexOutOfRange, the NullReference on run-before-init, and the same infinite loop for logN >= 32. ap_geodesicgrid.rs matches the tables, the float-widened Matrix3 (from_floats), the balance/zero_count switch, the (float) casts on w[i], is_zero on the widened float, the umbrella % 3 rotation and every branch of _from_neighbor_umbrella and _subtriangle_index. circularstream.rs keeps CanSeek true while Seek/Position/SetLength throw NotImplementedException. VersionDetection keeps the Groups[6][0] index bug (IndexOutOfRange when only the one-letter group matched). The regex crate keeps a repeated group's last participating capture as .NET does, so '4.5.0-rc2' gives group 4 = '0' and group 5 = '2'. version.rs has .NET Framework's two-to-four-part split, Int32 NumberStyles.Integer whitespace and sign handling, FormatException versus OverflowException, the -1 parts and component-wise CompareTo. R64-04's N2 now goes through format_fixed (15 significant digits, then half away from zero). Lost: (a) pelco.rs does not compile (R65-01); (b) Version::new does not validate build/revision and merges the 2/3/4-argument constructors, and Parse's ArgumentOutOfRange names 'version' where .NET Framework's VersionResult uses 'input'; (c) the cs_enum Display prints a number for combined [Flags] values where .NET prints 'IrisOpen, IrisClose'; (d) CircularStream.Read/Write with a short array panic in circularbuffer.rs instead of throwing IndexOutOfRangeException; (e) FFT2.init(31) aborts on allocation where C# throws OutOfMemoryException, and the comment at fft.rs:230 suggests a uint wrap that cannot happen; (f) the R64-03 fix leaves the read tag stale on three paths and starts loadwpsonconnect before the parameter download (R65-03); (g) setWPParams still ignores multiplierdist and TXT_loiterrad.Enabled and is not called from Activate. No new test covers the R64-03 or R64-04 changes.
scores.ui_ux_rationale: Unchanged, and only if R65-01 is fixed, because the app does not build as submitted. With 'Load Waypoints on connect' ticked the app now switches to Flight Plan and asks 'This will clear your existing points, Continue?' when the grid has rows, as MainV2 + BUT_read_Click do. A read timeout keeps the grid. But the failure only adds a 'Timeout getting waypoints' message line, where C#'s ProgressReporterDialogue shows the error. The view switch skips FlightPlanner.Activate. The firmware-update toast appears on every ArduPilot connect because no version is compared. The FFT window's spectra differ numerically from fftui's (no dB, a different window scale, mean removed). scores.features_rationale: Unchanged at 3.1, again only once R65-01 is fixed. Newly correct: loadwpsonconnect loads the vehicle's mission into the planner again; a read timeout no longer clears the planner's list; WP radius text rounds like N2 at decimal midpoints; the FFT butterfly is Mission Planner's. Still wrong or newly exposed: the connect-time rally ReadMission can silently replace the planner's in-flight read, and the tag then stays stale; the 'new firmware' check never compares versions, so it nags on every connect; Geo-Fence/Rally context Downloads still fill lists C# discards; integer parameters of 1e7 or more still lose digits on save; FFT output is not fftui's; setWPParams ignores the distance unit. VersionDetection, AP_GeodesicGrid, Pelco and CircularStream add no user-visible feature.

compile_check.summary: Checked every new and changed file against its definitions. fft.rs: dotnet::{index_out_of_range, Exception} exist (mod.rs:1517, 814); Exception::{NullReference, Overflow} exist; usize::try_from(i32) and i32::wrapping_mul/wrapping_shl and u32::wrapping_shl/wrapping_shr are fine; &mut Vec<f64> coerces to &mut [f64] in run; Option<usize>::is_some_and on a Copy value; m_X is &mut Vec<FFTElement> from as_mut()? and only borrowed immutably inside the closure; private FFTElement in a private field of pub FFT2 is allowed; derives are satisfied. The tests' &mut [0.0] coerces to &mut [f64]. ap_geodesicgrid.rs: Matrix3::from_floats is pub (matrix3.rs:37); Matrix3 is Copy, and Mul<Vector3> for Matrix3 (matrix3.rs:268) takes both by value, so inv[i] * *v moves copies out of the OnceLock array; Neg exists for Vector3T<T> (vector3.rs:481); Vector3 = Vector3T<f64> is Copy, so the test's -v after section(v, ..) is fine and Vector3::new resolves through the alias; OnceLock<[Matrix3; 10]> and OnceLock<[neighbor_umbrella; 3]> are Sync; the match arms '3 => return 0' and '0 => w.z = -w.z' type-check; the idx parameter shadows fn idx, which is allowed for functions. circularstream.rs: CircularBuffer<u8> satisfies Clone + Default + PartialEq and derives Debug/Clone; Stream: Send is satisfied; can_seek/position/length/read/write/flush are all trait items (mod.rs:1212-1237); Stream::read(&mut s, &mut b) coerces [u8; 4]. versiondetection.rs: regex and log are mp-core dependencies (Cargo.toml:12, 17); crate::dotnet::version is declared (mod.rs:20); Exception::Other exists (mod.rs:851); Version implements Display; the g closure returns &'h str tied to the haystack. version.rs: manual Ord with derived PartialEq/Eq compiles. link.rs: the new variant is constructed once (1871); every match over LinkEvent in the workspace (app.rs:523, flight_plan.rs:287, compass.rs:110) has a '_' arm, and all other uses (tests/*.rs, flight_data.rs, config.rs, setup.rs, mount.rs, vehicle_tuning.rs, demo.rs, forms.rs, firmware_ui.rs) are if-let or matches!. flight_plan.rs: the new fields are initialised in Default (249-250) and there is no other struct literal; the guard compares Option<u8> with Some(*mission_type). app.rs:657-660: link borrows only self.link, so assigning self.settings.view and calling self.flight_plan.but_read_click() after the loop is a disjoint borrow, and View is defined in app.rs:19. flight_data.rs:317: if-let with a literal field pattern through &LinkEvent is fine. tool_windows.rs: usize::trailing_zeros returns u32, and Exception implements Display (mod.rs:901). One definite error, in pelco.rs.

likely_errors.error: E0530: function parameters cannot shadow tuple structs. cs_enum! expands `cmd1` and `cmd2` to tuple structs (`pub struct cmd1(pub u8)`, dotnet/mod.rs:242), so their constructors are in the value namespace of this module, and the parameter patterns `cmd1: cmd1, cmd2: cmd2` in GenerateCommand are rejected (two errors). mp-core then fails to build, which takes mp-app and every test with it.
likely_errors.fix: Rename the bindings, e.g. `pub fn GenerateCommand(&self, cameraaddr: u8, command1: cmd1, command2: cmd2, data1: u8, data2: u8)`, and use `command1.0` / `command2.0` in the body. Add a comment that the C# parameter names cmd1/cmd2 cannot be kept in Rust.

low_confidence_risks: crates/mp-core/src/dotnet/mod.rs:573 (carried over): LCIDToLocaleName(langid as u32, Some(&mut buf), 0) assumes windows 0.62 folds lpName/cchName into Option<&mut [u16]>. If the binding takes (u32, PWSTR, i32, u32), write: LCIDToLocaleName(langid as u32, windows::core::PWSTR(buf.as_mut_ptr()), buf.len() as i32, 0).

crates/mp-core/src/extlibs/utilities/versiondetection.rs:79 (test, runtime): the '4.5.0-rc2' -> '4.5.0.2' assertion relies on the regex crate keeping group 4's capture from an earlier iteration of the outer '*' when a later iteration takes the '-rc' branch. regex-automata's engines do keep untouched slots, which matches .NET, but no other test in the repo pins this down.

findings.summary: R64-03 is partly fixed. A read timeout now emits MissionDownloadFailed, so the grid is kept, and Disconnected clears the tag. loadwpsonconnect again switches to Flight Plan, asks the confirm when rows exist, and reads into the planner. Remaining divergences: (1) the read starts on LinkEvent::Connected, before the parameter download, where C# runs it after getParamList. When ParamsLoaded later sends ReadMission{2} for RALLY_TOTAL > 0 (app.rs:619), link.rs:641 replaces the in-flight type-0 MissionOp without emitting anything. The planner then never gets its mission, awaiting_read stays Some(0), and the next type-0 download from Flight Data's Resume Mission is applied to the planner (the R63-03 bug). (2) A vehicle change (link.rs:804) and the pending-altitude refusal (link.rs:605) emit OperationError, not MissionDownloadFailed, so the tag also goes stale there. (3) The view switch is a plain assignment: MenuFlightPlanner_Click -> ShowScreen -> FlightPlanner.Activate (setWPParams etc.) is not run. (4) The setting is compared with == "True"; Settings.GetBoolean uses bool.TryParse, which ignores case and surrounding white space. (5) A failure adds only a 'Timeout getting waypoints' message line; C# shows the exception in the progress dialog. Flight Data's resume failure is silent. (6) The Geo-Fence/Rally context Downloads (menu.rs:434, 462 -> transfer -> mission_io) still load lists that C# discards. (7) No test was added.
findings.required_fix: Carry a request id on LinkCommand::ReadMission and LinkEvent::MissionDownloaded/MissionDownloadFailed, and have the link fail (not silently replace) a running MissionOp when a new one starts, as MAVLinkInterface's giveComport lock makes C# wait or throw. Emit MissionDownloadFailed for every aborted download. Run loadwpsonconnect after ParamsLoaded (or after the cache load) and before the rally fetch, through a View activation hook that also runs setWPParams. Parse the setting with bool.TryParse semantics. Make the context fence/rally Downloads discard their result. Add tests for: timeout keeps the grid; rally fetch during a planner read; loadwpsonconnect fills the grid; a stale tag after a vehicle change.

findings.cs_reference: Controls/fftui.cs:23-70, 172-302, 359-519, 604-719, 791-919 (fft.rin(buffer, (uint)bins, indB), fft.FreqTable(N, samplerate), FFT2.datastate); ExtLibs/Utilities/Spectrogram.cs:119-244
findings.summary: Only FFT2.init + run is wired. fftui calls rin, which applies the (4/N)*0.5*(1-cos) window and returns |X| or 20/ln10*ln(|X| + double.Epsilon) when indB, and FreqTable, whose bin frequencies are int-truncated (i*samplerate/N). spectra() subtracts the block mean, uses a 0.5-0.5cos window, divides by n, has no dB option and builds its own frequency axis, so every plotted value differs from Mission Planner. datastate is unused and Spectrogram.cs is not ported. fft() also passes trailing_zeros(n), which is only right for a power of two, and only logs a run error.
findings.required_fix: Port Controls/fftui.cs (its four handlers, the datastate accumulation and the indB checkbox) and Spectrogram.cs, and call FFT2::rin and FreqTable exactly as they do.

findings.summary: Small fidelity gaps in this round's support code. Version::new takes all four parts, checks only major/minor, and lets build/revision be any value; C# has three constructors, and the 3- and 4-argument ones throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException('build'/'revision'). Parse's ArgumentOutOfRange carries 'Parameter name: version', but .NET Framework's Version.Parse names 'input'. Int32.Parse's acceptance of trailing '\0' is not modelled. CircularStream.read_range/write_range panic (via circularbuffer.rs indexing) where C# throws IndexOutOfRangeException after a partial copy. FFT2.init(31) aborts on a 2^31-element allocation where C# throws OutOfMemoryException. The fft.rs:230 comment implies a uint wrap that cannot occur (start + spacing <= 2^32 - 1).
findings.required_fix: Split Version::new into new2/new3/new4 with C#'s checks and parameter names; use 'input' in Parse; make CircularBuffer's indexed copies return IndexOutOfRange; use try_reserve in FFT2::init and map failure to an OutOfMemory exception; fix the comment.

verdict: Five small ExtLibs/Utilities files (1,175 lines) were ported, and four of them are close statement-by-statement copies: FFT2 with its uint shifts, int FreqTable and double.Epsilon; AP_GeodesicGrid with the float-widened tables and float casts; CircularStream with CanSeek true and NotImplemented members; VersionDetection with its Groups[6] bug and a .NET Framework-style Version.Parse. The fifth, Pelco, breaks the build: GenerateCommand's parameters cmd1/cmd2 shadow the cs_enum tuple structs (E0530), so mp-core, the app and every test fail to compile. R64-03 and R64-04 are partly fixed. A read timeout no longer wipes the grid, loadwpsonconnect reaches the planner again, and N2 rounds like .NET. But the planner's read can still be silently replaced by the connect-time rally fetch, which leaves a stale tag, and setWPParams still ignores the distance unit and Activate. The new ports are mostly unwired. VersionDetection has no caller while the newer-firmware toast fires on every connect without comparing versions. The FFT window uses only the butterfly, not rin/FreqTable. Ported lines rise to 27,302 / 479,014 (5.7%); the cap stays 1.6. Awarded 1.1 (down 0.2 for the build break); round-file fidelity 5.9; UI/UX 2.2; features 3.1.
